description.narrative:
Stakeholder Effects: Improved access to affordable housing finance, including for women borrowers: IFC anticipates that the Project would help significantly increase access to affordable housing finance and encourage homeownership in the EWS and LIG segments, including for women borrowers. Rapid urbanization in India has led to serious development challenges including congestion, pressure on basic amenities, and severe housing shortages in cities, especially, in the low-cost segment. Housing financiers have been reluctant to finance the affordable segment due to the difficulties in assessing the debt servicing capacities of low- and middle-income group borrowers, and the high costs of servicing such loans. Within the affordable housing segment, women, especially those in lower and middle income groups, also remain an underserved segment.
Increased access to green affordable housing finance: Limited penetration of green housing is a key challenge in the Indian housing market. Along with IFCs investment, IFC will provide advisory support to Vastu to develop and grow its green housing portfolio from scratch, including creating a green housing framework.
Contribution to Market Creation: Competitiveness: IFCs investment and advisory support to Vastu, along with IFCs other systematic investment and advisory engagements in the segment with other companies, would help promote greater competitiveness in the affordable and green affordable housing market in India. Although IFC has been supporting the development of affordable housing financiers through continued interventions, the shortage of affordable housing is substantial and would require continuous support, including supporting the development of medium-sized regional NBFCs and HFCs that service lower and middle income groups. Developing green housing opportunities remains important given widespread climate concerns; however, few HFCs, including the large financiers, are focused on lending for green housing uni

The proposed project envisages an IFC own account equity investment of up to US$40 million in Vastu Housing Finance Corporation Limited (Vastu or the Company), a non-banking financial company housing finance company (NBFC-HFC), which provides affordable housing finance to lower and middle income segments and loans against properties (LAP) to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in India. IFCs primary equity investment will aid Vastu in further capitalizing the pick-up in credit growth in the affordable housing segment in the country post the waning of the Covid-19 pandemic. IFCs investment will also help the Company offer green affordable housing loans to its customers, enhance their micro-housing and gender offerings, and improve their environmental and social (E&S) and climate risk governance.
